name: Follow the Queen
description: Follow the Queen is one of the most unpredictable and chaotic variations of Seven Card Stud. While it follows the standard Stud structure, it introduces a roving wild card mechanic that can change mid-hand. The core rule is that Queens are wild, and the rank of the card dealt immediately after a Queen (the 'Trailer') also becomes wild. This creates massive hand rankings where Five-of-a-Kind is not just possible, but frequent, and the lead can shift dramatically with a single card deal.

history.origins: A popular home game variant from the mid-20th century, Follow the Queen was designed to inject high volatility into the otherwise methodical game of Seven Card Stud. It is a staple of 'Dealer's Choice' poker nights across North America.
timeline: 1950s: Emerges in domestic poker circles as a way to inflate pots and increase action.
1970s: Becomes a standard 'Wild Card' variant in informal casinos and home games.
Present: Frequently played in recreational poker leagues as a 'fun' alternative to serious tournament formats.
history.cultural: Symbolizes the 'wild' side of American social poker, where the focus is on large pots and surprising reversals.
history.evolution: As Poker strategy became more refined, Follow the Queen remained popular because its shifting wild cards actively disrupt modern mathematical modeling, making it a game of pure intuition and adaptation.

setup.dealing: Standard Seven Card Stud deal: 2 down, 4 up, 1 down.

rules.objective: Win the pot by forming the highest-ranking 5-card Poker hand using any of the seven cards dealt, utilizing the current wild cards.
rules.gameplay:
1. Initial Deal: 2 down, 1 up. Betting.
2. 4th, 5th, 6th Streets: One upcard each, with a betting round after each. If a Queen is dealt, watch the next card closely!
3. The River: One final down-card. Final betting round.
keyRules: Natural is Better: In some house rules, a 'Natural' hand (without wild cards) beats a wild hand of the same rank.
No Queen No Game: If no Queen appears face-up by the end of dealing, many play that there are NO wild cards, or that the hand is a 'misdeal' and everyone re-antes.
Winning condition: Win the pot by forming the highest-ranking 5-card Poker hand using any of the seven cards dealt, utilizing the current wild cards.

strategy.basic: Don't get attached to your hand until the 6th card is dealt. A pair of Aces is great, but if 9s suddenly become wild on the 6th street, you might be instantly losing to a Three-of-a-Kind.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Queen Hunt': If you are looking for a specific rank to fill a Straight, hoping for a Queen to appear can be a viable strategy, as it effectively doubles your 'outs'.
strategy.advanced: Psychology of Shifting Wilds: If the wild card changes late in the hand, players who were betting aggressively on the previous wild card will often go into 'check' mode. Use this hesitation to bluff if you can represent the new wild card.
tips: Always keep track of which Queens have already been dealt. If 3 Queens are on the table, the wild card is unlikely to change again.
Five-of-a-Kind: Remember that with wild cards, a 'Five-of-a-Kind' is the highest possible hand, beating even a Royal Flush.

scoring.description: Points scored through betting rounds and won by highest Poker hand at showdown. Cash game or chip-based play.
scoring.winCondition: Player with the highest 5-card Poker hand from their 7 cards wins the pot. With Five-of-a-Kind (wild cards + naturals) ranking highest.

synthesis.shortDescription: A volatile Seven Card Stud variant where Queens and their immediate followers are wild, creating dramatic hand strength reversals mid-hand.
